1: The 'No, really?' mocks research that 'proves' what everyone already knows, like the chocolate and blonde examples. The author goes on to agree with the finding — D.
2: Twice the money with more misery shows only that wealth doesn't necessarily bring happiness — A. It says nothing about children specifically or about less wealth making them happier.
3: Kahneman's link is that success takes time and energy away from other things. It needn't assume shorter hours give children more time (1). It needn't assume failure is stress-free (2). Neither — D.
4: The support is one story about a family the author knows and a two-year-old. That's anecdotal evidence — B.
5: The argument finds extreme sports puzzling, because sport is meant to relieve the pressures of work. If people want to escape the safety obsession at work, risky sport makes sense — B.
6: J months: Jan, Jun, Jul. A: Apr, Aug. M: Mar, May. Alice–Michael 5 months apart: only Aug–Mar works. Jenny 2 months from August: June. June to March = 3 months — C.
7: The argument says lack of sleep causes memory loss. Memory loss could cause poor sleep instead (1), or ageing could cause both (3). Individual variation (2) doesn't touch the causal claim — D.
8: In September the month is 09. The other three numbers must be different non-zero squares other than 9. Hour: 01, 04, 16 (3). Day: 01, 04, 16, 25 excluding the hour (3). Minute: 01, 04, 16, 25, 36, 49 excluding both (4). 3 × 3 × 4 = 36 — B.

10: A circle inside one square, or one whose pieces line up with the pattern, can use the existing colours. But a circle crossing squares can create regions that touch both colours, so it needs a third colour. Never more than one extra — C.
11: Any map made only from straight lines that cross the whole island can be coloured with 2 colours: swap the colours on one side of each line. 2 always suffice — A.
12: Each pyramid's 5 side faces form a ring of 5, an odd number, so 2 colours can't alternate around it. 3 colours do work — B.
13: Compare tiles by their pattern of black and white (allowing rotations). Corner, edge and centre tiles of the motifs give 8 distinct types — D.
14: The argument is that lower consumption needs higher prices. If Scottish consumption doubled as prices fell, price clearly drives consumption — B.

17: If Beth is unmarried, married Al is looking at her. If Beth is married, she is looking at unmarried Charles. Either way the answer is yes — C.
